title: Carboplatin every 3 weeks with head and neck radiotherapy
context_label: Locally advanced stage III–IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is not appropriate.
indication_text: Locally advanced stage III–IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is not appropriate.
purpose: Carboplatin is given with radiotherapy to treat locally advanced head and neck cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable. Your team explains the intended chance of cure or long-term control for your diagnosis.
schedule_summary: Carboplatin is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 21 days. The head and neck prescription uses AUC 5, a target used with your checked kidney function to calculate the dose. The whole visit includes safety checks, anti-sickness medicines, preparation and observation. Three carboplatin cycles are planned with concurrent radiotherapy. Radiation has a separate appointment calendar; the team coordinates any interruptions or changes.
administration_text: Carboplatin is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 21 days. The head and neck prescription uses AUC 5, a target used with your checked kidney function to calculate the dose. The whole visit includes safety checks, anti-sickness medicines, preparation and observation.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests before every cycle. The team verifies the current kidney result and dose calculation, and reviews infection, bleeding, hearing and nerve symptoms.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with DNA copying and repair. This can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, and kidney function determines how the medicine is cleared.
agents.watch: Contact the oncology emergency service immediately for fever or shaking chills, sudden illness, bleeding, new breathlessness, chest pain or severe allergy. Report reduced urine, hearing changes and new numbness promptly. Do not wait for the next visit.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Infusion allergy, particularly with repeat platinum exposure
Fertility effects and harm to an unborn baby

agents.name: Radiotherapy
agents.mechanism: Damages cancer cells in the planned treatment area
agents.explanation: Radiotherapy directs radiation at a carefully planned area. It is delivered on its own appointment calendar. Effects depend on which tissues receive radiation and can build up during the course or continue after it finishes.
agents.watch: Report difficulty swallowing, weight loss, mouth pain, skin breakdown or problems managing saliva.
risks: Dry mouth, taste and saliva changes
Skin reaction in the treated area
Some swallowing, saliva or tissue effects can be lasting

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Checks blood cells and helps assess infection, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each treatment cycle

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Checks organ function; kidney function is also used to calculate carboplatin dose.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each cycle

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney-function measurement
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Provides the renal value needed for the carboplatin dose calculation; measured function is preferred when feasible.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Baseline and repeat or reassess when clinically required; estimated dosing needs a current creatinine result.

monitoring_test_details.label: Scans and head and neck examination
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assesses the cancer and the response to treatment separately from safety bloods.
monitoring_test_details.timing: As prescribed in the individual disease-assessment plan

support.title: Anti-sickness medicines
support.text: This carboplatin regimen has high sickness risk. Take the prescribed prevention and rescue medicines on their written schedule. Call if nausea or vomiting prevents drinking.

support.title: Eating and weight
support.text: Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.

support.title: Mouth and dental care
support.text: Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.

support.title: Swallowing and communication
support.text: Ask for speech and language therapy if swallowing or speech is difficult. Use the food textures, exercises and communication support advised for you; a general guide cannot establish safe swallowing.

support.title: Medicines and fertility
support.text: Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Carboplatin can impair fertility. Do not breastfeed during treatment. The linked Irish product information advises contraception for women during treatment and at least six months afterwards; men should avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least three months afterwards. Confirm the actual product and personal advice.

items.text: Your team weighs the cancer, previous treatment, health, symptoms and preferences when discussing options. Other systemic treatment, local treatment where suitable, trials or symptom-focused care may be discussed.

items.text: Blood results, kidney function or side effects may delay or change a dose. The chemotherapy and radiation teams coordinate the plan; do not use an old appointment list as authority to restart.

chapters.title: Recognising side effects
chapters.intro: Use the anatomical map with these explanations; location does not tell you how urgent a symptom is.

items.title: Hearing / tinnitus
items.text: Report hearing change or ringing in the ears; previous platinum treatment increases risk.

items.title: Mouth / throat / saliva
items.text: Mouth pain, thick saliva, dry mouth or swallowing difficulty can limit drinking; seek help early.

items.title: Blood cells / infection
items.text: Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding needs prompt oncology advice.

items.title: Kidneys / fluids
items.text: Kidney tests guide the carboplatin dose. Much less urine, persistent vomiting or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

items.title: Nausea / appetite
items.text: Take the prescribed prevention and rescue medicines. Call if vomiting persists or fluids will not stay down.

items.title: Nerves / hands / feet
items.text: Report numbness, tingling, balance problems or difficulty with fine tasks; symptoms can persist.

items.title: Skin / treated area
items.text: Follow the radiation team’s skin plan. Report painful redness, peeling or a wound that is not healing.

items.title: Teeth / jaw / swallowing
items.text: Dental review, nutrition and swallowing support continue through recovery. Report jaw stiffness, weight loss or choking.

chapters.title: When and how to get help
chapters.intro: Use the oncology service’s written urgent-contact plan.

items.title: Contact the team promptly
items.text: Contact oncology promptly for fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bleeding, persistent vomiting, much less urine or inability to drink. Report worsening hearing, numbness or tingling before the next dose. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or severe chest pain is an emergency.

items.title: During an infusion or injection
items.text: Tell staff immediately about itching, a rash, dizziness, chest tightness, breathing difficulty, pain or swelling around the treatment site.

items.title: Prepare the handover
items.text: Tell the clinician the medicine name, date of the last dose, new symptoms and any prescribed steroids or hormone replacement. Carry the wallet card; do not delay urgent care while looking for a document.

chapters.title: Eating, mouth care and everyday support
chapters.intro: Ask for help before a practical problem prevents treatment.

items.title: Mouth and dental care

items.title: Swallowing and communication
items.text: Ask for individual speech and language therapy advice for swallowing or communication difficulties. Report choking, coughing with drinks or inability to swallow safely.

items.title: Energy and activity
items.text: Plan manageable activity and rest around symptoms. Tell the team about severe or unexpected fatigue, falls or difficulties managing at home.

chapters.title: Medicines, precautions and visit preparation
chapters.intro: Review medicines and practical needs before treatment.

items.title: Medicines and fertility
items.text: Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Carboplatin can impair fertility. items.title: Access and observation
items.text: Your team chooses suitable venous access for an infusion. A port, if used, has its own insertion, care and removal plan; it is not removed after each visit. No take-home chemotherapy pump is part of this regimen.

items.title: Work, transport and communication
items.text: Discuss transport, work, caring responsibilities, interpreter needs and a support person. Ask how results and changes will be communicated and who books your next tests.

chapters.title: Your record and contact card
chapters.intro: Keep the information that another clinician would need.

items.title: Cycle or review record
items.text: Record the cycle received, date, route, dose if supplied, important symptoms, any hold and the next agreed review. Stamp boxes record treatment received; they do not authorise the next dose.

items.title: Contacts and documents
items.text: Have the team replace example telephone numbers with your actual daytime and out-of-hours contacts. Carry the front/back wallet card and immune alert card when applicable. The printed handbook contains the key information without needing to scan a QR code.

items.title: Questions for review
items.text: Bring your main question, changes in swallowing or weight, symptoms, medicine changes and any concerns about the treatment aim. Ask for the plan in words you can explain back.

chapters.title: Evidence and further information
chapters.intro: Use evidence to support a personal treatment discussion.

items.title: What studies can tell us
items.text: The NCCP regimen includes carboplatin with radiation when cisplatin is inappropriate. Its cited head and neck comparison is a matched-pair analysis; this does not establish randomised equivalence to cisplatin for every patient.

items.title: Your individual decision
items.text: Group results cannot predict what will happen for you. Ask which benefits matter for your situation and how the team will decide whether treatment remains worthwhile.

items.title: Resources
items.text: The source list gives the official regimen and public patient information. Ask your team for a printed copy or help accessing a resource if needed.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Carboplatin is given with radiotherapy to treat locally advanced head and neck cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable. Your team explains the intended chance of cure or long-term control for your diagnosis.
evidence.population: Locally advanced stage III–IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is not appropriate.
evidence.comparison: A matched-pair analysis cited by NCCP; patient selection matters.
evidence.interpretation: The NCCP regimen includes carboplatin with radiation when cisplatin is inappropriate. Its cited head and neck comparison is a matched-pair analysis; this does not establish randomised equivalence to cisplatin for every patient.
limitations: Trial results describe groups; your individual benefit and risks may differ.
Do not transfer survival estimates between different cancer settings, schedules or treatment combinations.

consent_support: Discuss your diagnosis, intent, alternatives, expected benefit and uncertainty, treatment burden, serious or lasting harms, fertility and pregnancy precautions and your priorities. Include blood-count suppression, serious infection and bleeding, nausea/vomiting, allergy, renal dose calculation, hearing and nerve effects, and the separate radiotherapy consent covering mouth, saliva, skin, dental, jaw and swallowing effects. Confirm actual urgent contacts and use teach-back. This draft does not authorise treatment.
